title: 03 · Bug hunt
summary: Errors, warnings and silent bugs; eight messages R prints and what each means; a proofreading checklist and a script with six bugs.
question: When R misbehaves, how do you tell what went wrong and fix it?

chain.title: Errors stop R
chain.statement: An error stops R at the failing line and prints a message in red that names the problem.

explain.text: Nothing after the failing line runs, so the first error is the one to read and fix; later lines may only fail because of it. The message usually names the object, function or file involved, which tells you where to look.

figure.caption: Three kinds of trouble, from loud to silent.

nodes.label: Silent bug: wrong answer, no message

terms.meaning: R cannot run the line and stops

chain.intuition: An error is a fire alarm: loud, and it stops everything.

intuitionFigure.caption: R runs line by line until the first error.

chain.misconception: The last error printed is the one to fix. Fix the first one: later errors often follow from it.

wrong.title: Mistaken
wrong.text: Start with the last red line.

right.title: Instead
right.text: Start with the first red line; re-run.

check.q: Line 2 fails with "object 'dat' not found" and line 5 fails too. Which do you fix first?
check.a: Line 2: line 5 may only fail because dat was never created.

chain.opens: What is a warning, and why is it more dangerous than it looks?
chain.answers: When R misbehaves, how do you tell what went wrong and fix it?

chain.title: Warnings: R ran, but check
chain.statement: A warning means R finished the line but suspects the result; the output exists and may be wrong.

explain.text: mean("ten") from sheet 01 is the model case: R returns NA and warns that the argument is not numeric. The script goes on, so a warning can carry a bad value into everything after it unless you read it.

terms.meaning: R ran the line but flags a likely problem with the result

chain.intuition: A warning is the amber light: you may go, but look first.

right.title: Instead
right.text: Warning = a result exists but may be wrong.

chain.misconception: Warnings can be ignored if the script finishes.

wrong.title: Mistaken
wrong.text: No red stop → result is fine.

right.title: Instead
right.text: Read every warning; check the value it produced.

check.q: as.numeric(c("1", "two")) gives 1 NA with a warning. What happened?
check.a: "two" could not be converted, so it became NA; R warns that NAs were introduced.

chain.opens: What is worse than an error or a warning?
chain.answers: What is a warning, and why is it more dangerous than it looks?

chain.title: Silent bugs: no message, wrong answer
chain.statement: A silent bug runs without any message and gives a wrong answer; only checking the result reveals it.

explain.text: Examples: a formula written the wrong way round (TotalSleep ~ Danger versus Danger ~ TotalSleep), the wrong column picked, a filter that dropped half the rows. R cannot know your intention, so it cannot warn you; compare each result with what you expect (sign, size, n).

terms.meaning: code that runs cleanly but does not do what you meant

chain.intuition: A silent bug is a wrong turn with no sign: you only notice by checking the map.

intuitionFigure.caption: The only defence: check the result.

chain.misconception: No red text means the code is correct.

right.title: Instead
right.text: No message → still check n, sign and size.

check.q: mean(dat$BodyWt) gives 198.8 kg for mammals that are mostly small. Bug?
check.a: Not necessarily a bug: the mean is pulled up by elephants; the median shows the typical mammal. Check before you trust it.

wrong.title: Mistaken
wrong.text: A strange number means a bug.

right.title: Instead
right.text: A strange number means: look at the data (skew, units).

chain.opens: What do the most common red messages mean?
chain.answers: What is worse than an error or a warning?

chain.title: Object or function not found
chain.statement: R found nothing with that exact name: names are case-sensitive, so Dat is not dat; and "could not find function Mean" means a misspelt function or a package not loaded.

explain.text: Check the spelling and the capitals, or run the line that creates the object first. For a function, check the name (mean, not Mean) and run library() for its package.

lines.explain: Dat does not exist: Error: object 'Dat' not found
the object created by read.csv() is called dat

code.interpret: The name must match exactly, capitals included.

terms.meaning: capitals matter: dat, Dat and DAT are three different names

chain.intuition: R reads names letter by letter, capitals included.

wrong.title: Mistaken
wrong.text: R will find dat when I type Dat.

right.title: Instead
right.text: R stops: nothing is called Dat.

check.a: Write mean(x) (lower case); or, if Mean comes from a package, load it with library().

chain.opens: Why can R not open a file or a package that exists?
chain.answers: What do the most common red messages mean?

chain.title: File and package not found

quote.text: cannot open file 'sleep.csv': No such file or directory

chain.statement: The file is not where R is looking (the working directory); and "there is no package called viridislite" means not installed, or misspelt (it is viridisLite).

explain.text: Run getwd() to see where R looks, then setwd() or open your R Project. For a package, check the exact spelling, run install.packages() once, then library().

lines.explain: move R to the folder with the file

code.interpret: Folder and spelling cause almost all "not found" messages.

terms.meaning: a folder file (.Rproj) that sets the working directory for you

chain.intuition: R only searches one drawer: the working directory.
chain.misconception: If the file is on my computer, R can open it.

right.title: Instead
right.text: R searches the working directory only.

check.q: library(ggplot) fails but ggplot2 is installed. Why?
check.a: The package is called ggplot2: names must match exactly.

chain.answers: Why can R not open a file or a package that exists?

chain.title: Unexpected symbols and brackets
chain.statement: An unexpected ")" means the brackets do not pair up; an unexpected symbol means two things stand side by side with nothing between, usually a missing comma.

explain.text: Every ( needs exactly one ); every argument is separated by a comma. R prints the code up to the point where it got confused, so the fault is just before the end of what it shows.

lines.explain: missing comma between x and na.rm: unexpected symbol
corrected: one closing bracket, and a comma between the arguments

code.interpret: The quoted fragment ends where R stopped understanding.

terms.meaning: the line is not valid R, so it cannot even start

chain.intuition: R reads like a strict proofreader and stops at the first mismatch.

intuitionFigure.caption: Brackets must pair: one ( for each ).

chain.misconception: The error is at the end of the quoted code. It is just before: R shows where it gave up.

right.title: Instead
right.text: Look at what comes just before it: a missing comma or bracket.

check.q: sd(x na.rm = TRUE) fails. What is missing?

chain.opens: What does "non-numeric argument" mean, and what is the + prompt?

chain.title: Maths on text, and the waiting +

quote.text: Error in dat$Species + 1 : non-numeric argument to binary operator

chain.statement: Arithmetic on a text column fails: Species is chr. A + at the start of the console line means R is waiting for you to close an open ( or ".

explain.text: Run str(dat) to see which columns are chr. For the +, press Esc, close the bracket or quote, and run the line again.

lines.explain: Species holds names (text): arithmetic is impossible

output: Error in dat$Species + 1 : non-numeric argument to binary operator

terms.meaning: R is waiting for the rest of an unfinished line

chain.misconception: The + prompt means R is adding.

right.title: Instead
right.text: + = your line is unfinished: close ( or ".

check.q: The console shows + after mean(x, na.rm = TRUE. What is missing?

chain.opens: What should you check before you even run a line?
chain.answers: What does "non-numeric argument" mean, and what is the + prompt?

chain.title: Proofread before you run
chain.statement: Ten checks catch most bugs before they happen: spelling and capitals, packages loaded, straight quotes, pairs closed, the right folder, the formula way round, commas, data types, the right function and NAs handled.

explain.text: TotalSleep is not totalsleep; library() runs every session; quotes copied from a PDF are often curly (“ ”) and R needs straight ones; every ( and " has a partner; getwd() before read.csv(); a formula is response ~ group; arguments are separated by commas; str() after every import; ?name to check the function; na.rm = TRUE where NAs exist.

figure.caption: The ten checks of the proofreading list.

terms.meaning: typographic quotes “ ” that R does not accept as string delimiters

chain.intuition: A pilot's checklist: boring, quick, and it prevents crashes.
chain.misconception: Code copied from a PDF will run as it is. Curly quotes and odd dashes often break it.

check.q: boxplot(Danger ~ TotalSleep) runs but looks wrong. Which check fails?
check.a: The formula is the wrong way round: it should be TotalSleep ~ Danger (response ~ group).

chain.opens: Can you find the six bugs in a short script?
chain.answers: What should you check before you even run a line?

chain.title: Spot the bugs: a six-line script
chain.statement: The six-line script has six bugs: a misspelt package, a missing quote, a wrong capital, a wrong column name, missing NA handling, and a formula the wrong way round.

explain.text: Line 1 loads viridislite but the package is viridisLite. Line 2 lacks the closing " after .csv. Line 3 inspects Dat, but the object is dat. Line 4 averages totalsleep, but the column is TotalSleep, and it needs na.rm = TRUE. Line 5 puts the formula backwards: sleep is the response, so TotalSleep ~ Danger.

figure.caption: The script and its fixes, line by line.

code.interpret: With all six fixes the script runs and the mean is the 10.53 h of sheet 01.

terms.meaning: formula order: the measured outcome on the left, the grouping on the right

chain.intuition: Bugs hide in names, pairs and order.
chain.misconception: Fixing the first error is enough. Each fix lets R reach the next bug; re-run after every fix.

right.title: Instead
right.text: Fix the first error, re-run, read the next message.

check.q: Which of the six bugs would give no message at all?
check.a: The backwards formula (line 5): it draws a plot, just the wrong one.

right.title: Instead
right.text: Line 5 runs silently and draws the wrong plot.

chain.opens: What do you do when you cannot see the bug?
chain.answers: Can you find the six bugs in a short script?
